| [NOTE-020](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-020.md) v2 | Emergence as the conversion of information | Varley and Hoel apply a PID, with the Williams–Beer I_min redundancy, to past→future mutual information and summarise it with a new layer-weighted "synergy bias" B_syn ∈ [0,1]. | [NOTE-032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-032.md) v2 | Work capacity of channels with memory | The paper models agent and environment as coupled finite hidden-Markov channels. It defines the environment's work capacity C_work = max over agent models of ⟨H(A_t\|M_t) − H(S_t\|M_t)⟩_t (in k_BT ln 2 per round) and proves two things. First, for unifilar environments whose percepts ignore actions, the efficient agents are exactly the randomize-and-forget ∩ maximally-predictive ones, and C_work = log\|A\| − h(S). Second, one binary memoryless environment exists where predictive, max-entropy-action and efficient agents form three nonempty, pairwise-disjoint sets: every predictive agent extracts ≤ 0, uniform-random agents extract 1 − h(3/4) ≈ 0.189 bits, and the optimum is ½·log₂(3/4 + 1/√2) ≈ 0.272 bits, reached by a memoryless agent that plays action 0 with probability 1/√2. | Read |

| [NOTE-045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-045.md) v2 | Gutknecht et al. 2025, Shannon invariants | For any set of quantities Π(α) satisfying the PID consistency equation (A7), whatever the redundancy measure, two averages are fixed by Shannon quantities alone. They are the average degree of redundancy, r̄ = Σᵢ I(Xᵢ;Y)/I(X;Y) (Prop. 1), and the average degree of vulnerability, v̄ = Σⱼ I(Xⱼ;Y\|X₋ⱼ)/I(X;Y) (Prop. 2). Two identities follow: RSI = (r̄ − 1)·I(X;Y) (Cor. 1), and a new "dual" index DRSI = I(X;Y) − Σⱼ I(Xⱼ;Y\|X₋ⱼ) = (1 − v̄)·I(X;Y) (Prop. 4, Cor. 2). In small, stochastically quantised (8-level) networks analysed on their own training set, r̄ about the label rises with depth and v̄ falls with depth and training. In a face autoencoder, decoder layers are more redundant than size-matched encoder layers, and r̄ rises with bottleneck width. | Read |
| [NOTE-046](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-046.md) v2 | Chu & Raginsky, expected soft maxima of Gaussian processes | Take a centered Gaussian process on a finite set T with max variance σ² and minimum separation a. For β ≥ β*, g(β) ≥ c·a·√(E D(ν_β‖ν₀)), with c the Sudakov constant (1/17 via Marcus–Rosen) (Thm 2). For i.i.d. N(0,σ²) logits there is an exact identity, g(β) = βσ²(1 − E‖ν_β‖²₂) (Lemma 2). | [NOTE-053](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-053.md) v2 | Transfer entropy as a log-likelihood ratio | For a parametric Markov model f(x_t \| x^k_t, y^k_t; θ) of X, the likelihood-ratio estimator T̂ = −(1/(n−k)) log Λ for the null "no dependence on Y's past" converges almost surely to the transfer entropy T_{Y→X} (Theorem 1a). Under the null, 2(n−k)T̂ is asymptotically χ²(d), with d the difference in parameter counts (Theorem 1b). | [NOTE-088](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-088.md) | The Homological Nature of Entropy | On a finite probability space, take an information structure S (a set of partitions closed under joins that have a common refinement in S and containing the trivial partition) and a probability family Q complete for it. The information cohomology H*(S;Q) is computed by a Hochschild-type bar complex whose action is Shannon's averaged conditioning. If S is connected and "sufficiently rich" and cochains are measurable, then H¹ is one-dimensional and spanned by Shannon entropy (Thm 1). This makes entropy the unique measurable 1-cocycle, up to one multiplicative constant per connected component. In the unitary-invariant quantum case H¹_U = 0: Shannon entropy is the coboundary of minus the von Neumann entropy, which is the unique invariant 0-cochain with that property up to an additive constant (Thm 3). The tree ("arborescent") version again gives H¹ spanned by entropy (Thm 4). | Read |
| [NOTE-096](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-096.md) v2 | Karpenko — Defending informational structural realism | Karpenko argues against V.E. | [NOTE-099](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-099.md) v2 | Floridi — A defence of informational structural realism | Floridi argues informally in four steps. (1) ESR and (non-eliminativist) OSR are compatible once indexed to levels of abstraction. ESR's minimal commitment to knowable relations holds at a first-order LoA. At a reflective ("transcendental") second-order LoA, a second Ockham principle licenses taking the relata to be structural objects. (2) The relata-need-relations regress is blocked by Eddington's "package hypothesis": not all relata are logically prior to relations. (3) Structural objects are informational objects, clusters of data understood as concrete "differentiae de re", made scalable by the object-oriented-programming model. (4) Together these give "informational structural realism", on which "the ultimate nature of reality is informational" (p. 32). | Read |

| [NOTE-122](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-122.md) v2 | Barrett et al. — IIT: good, bad and misunderstood | A position paper with no new formal result. It argues four things. IIT's algorithm is undefined whenever any spatial, temporal or state graining of a system is non-Markovian (Barrett & Mediano 2019), and so gives no output for brains; it cannot handle unbounded continuous state variables; and it has never been computed on any real system. PCI and other "approximations" of Φ are proxies, capturing at most two of the six axioms. The theory would need recasting in continuous fields (the EM field) to fit the standard model. Against critics, the authors hold that IIT can be read with a multi-dimensional measure of global state (mean Φ, variance of cause-effect-structure quantities, structural complexity), on which Aaronson's inactive expander grid is only minimally conscious, and that IIT's implied "tiling" panpsychism is no worse than any rival metaphysics. | Read |

| [NOTE-190](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-190.md) | Real Patterns | A pattern is real in some data "if there is a description of the data that is more efficient than the bit map, whether or not anyone can concoct it" (p. 34). | [NOTE-241](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-241.md) | ZipNN | Lossless compression of trained-model files works almost entirely through the float exponent. It is concentrated on about 40 of 256 values, the top 12 hold ~99.9% of parameters, and it compresses to ~33% under order-0 Huffman coding, while sign and mantissa stay ≈100%. So "regular" BF16 models compress to ~66.4% and FP32 models to ~83%. Rounded "clean" models reach 33.7–48.1%, and ZipNN (exponent extraction plus Huffman only) beats vanilla Zstd by 17% in size and 62% in single-thread speed on Llama-3.1-8B BF16. The paper never computes an entropy and never compares its codes to one. | Read |
